items.title: Bob Haggart interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: my two favorite bass players were Pops Foster... and Artie Bernstein, who I happened to hear along about that time... I was very impressed with that.

ctx.x: You are a stellar bassist. When did you start playing the string bass, and what led you to that instrument?

Well I was, I started playing in high school actually. But before that I was a guitar player and played the special tuning, they don’t use it today, it’s a four string instrument with a tenor banjo tuning and then the strings were inverted so that the bottom string was up an octave and the top string was down an octave, which made it more like a ukulele in other words, close tuning. And I studied with George VanEps at that time, who is, he was playing that particular instrument and starting on the regular six…

both of those guys. In those days bass was sort of part of the rhythm section and you never heard from them hardly any solos. The only who was playing solos in those days was Milt Hinton with Cab Calloway’s band, and Milt, he was the first really well known bassist, outside of perhaps Red Brown, who played with the Goldkette band, Steve Brown, called Steve “Red” Brown. He joined after Jean Goldkette, he went with Paul Whiteman. And that was the first recording where you could really hear the bass. Up to that time…
